nf16e13.title: The Check-In Word
nf16e13.caption: Walking into a loud family gathering can be a lot. Agree on one check-in word before you go in: it means "check on me," and you step out together. Save this for your next visit.

nf16e14.title: The Ex Question
nf16e14.caption: When someone asks about your ex in front of your new partner, you don't owe the whole story. Keep it short, keep it kind, then bring the conversation back to now.

nf16e15.title: Quiet Isn't Unhappy
nf16e15.caption: If your partner goes quiet at your family's table, try not to guess what it means. Ask them in private and offer a break. Some people enjoy the room by listening.

nf16e16.title: The Baby Photos
nf16e16.caption: The baby photos came out. Laugh along, it's how families say they love you. One kind "okay, last one" is fine, and partners, be sweet about it. Who has the most embarrassing album?

nf16e17.title: Offer to Help
nf16e17.caption: Want to help at your partner's family dinner? Offer once, warmly. If they say no, believe them, then find a small job like the dishes. Help the way they like help.

nf16e18.title: Not in the Guest Room
nf16e18.caption: Tension during a holiday stay is normal. Skip the whisper-fight in the guest room: name it, take a walk together, and talk it through outside the house.

nf16e19.title: Back Them Up
nf16e19.caption: If a relative teases your partner, back them up in the moment, with a calm voice and no scene. Then check in with them later. Tag someone who always has your back.

nf16e20.title: Homesick at Their Table
nf16e20.caption: Your first holiday away from your own family can feel bittersweet, even at a warm table. It's okay to miss home out loud. Make a little room for both.

nf16e21.title: The Family Photo
nf16e21.caption: Not sure if you belong in their family photo? Just ask. "In or out?" is a kind question, and either answer is fine. Send this to someone meeting the family this year.

nf16e22.title: The Drive Home
nf16e22.caption: On the drive home from their family's, start with three things you genuinely liked. Then share one honest thing, gently. Their family, their call.

nf16e23.title: The Thank-You Text
nf16e23.caption: After a visit, thank their parents within a day. Use their name and mention one real moment. Small, specific thanks are the ones people keep.

nf16e24.title: Our Own Tradition
nf16e24.caption: After all the visits, ask what the two of you want to keep. Keep what felt like home, gently let go of what didn't, and start one tradition that's just yours. What would yours be?
